##: The manifest for the author's bucket, https://github.com/ruslan-rv-ua/scoop-bucket. This
copy is the seed: it went into the bucket as bucket/revisor.json once, by hand, after the
first release (the Backlog document «Випуск релізу»), with the real hash from that
release's .sha256 in place of the zeros below. From then on the bucket's own Excavator
bumps the bucket's copy from the checkver and autoupdate fields; nothing bumps this one.
Excavator changes versions and hashes only, never the shape: when a release changes the
shape, as 0.5.0 did by adding revisor-cli.exe, the bucket's copy is brought to this shape
by hand once more, with that release's version and hashes (the same document).
Two files per release (ADR-0015): revisor.exe, the window, and revisor-cli.exe, the
command line. The '#/revisor.exe' and '#/revisor-cli.exe' fragments rename the downloads,
so 'bin' and the shortcut stay the same across versions while the release files keep
their versions in their names. scoop strips the fragment before it downloads.
A GUI exe needs nothing special: scoop makes the shim a GUI program when its target is
one, so starting revisor from PATH flashes no console. The shim of revisor-cli.exe is a
console program like its target, so a script waits for it and gets its exit code.
'shortcuts' adds 'revisor' to the Start menu; the command line gets no shortcut.
revisor keeps everything it writes in a 'data' folder beside its exes, which both exes
share. 'persist' links <app>\data to ~\scoop\persist\revisor\data with a junction, so
settings, profiles and snapshots survive 'scoop update' and 'scoop uninstall' without
--purge.
autoupdate takes each hash from its file's .sha256 sidecar: '$url' there is the download
URL of the file in turn, without its '#/' fragment, so '$url.sha256' is the sidecar
beside it, and its '<hex64> *<name>' line is what scoop's hash extraction reads. One hash
template serves both URLs: scoop reuses the last template for every URL after it.
description: Folder snapshots that show what a program created, changed or deleted, made for the keyboard and screen readers
